Manuscript, pen-and-ink. Oriented with north to the right. Relief shown pictorially. "This is a copy of the first map engraved in New England. Taken from one in Hubbard's Narrative of the troubles with the Indians in New England, supposed to have been published in 1677." "The figures that are joyned with the names of places are to distinguish such as have been assaulted by Indians from others." Imperfect: Legend in lower margin largely wanting. Scale ca. 1:900,000. Available also through the Library of Congress Web site as a raster image. Vault AACR2
Oriented with north to the right.
dct_title_s: A map of New-England, being the first that ever was here cut, and done by the best pattern that could be had, which being in some places defective, it made the other less exact: Yet doth it sufficiently show the situation of the country & conveniently well the distances of places
